name: Kingdom of Italy

areaKm2.note: Published area ~286,600 km2 (B&H Table 1: 0.3M km2); the world_1914 Kingdom of Italy polygon computes to ~293,000 km2 (high).

population.note: Broadberry and Harrison 2005 Table 1: Italy 1913 = 35.6M (low); COW tpop 1915 = 36,390k (high); OWID/HYDE 1915 = 36.43M. Libya and other colonies (2.0M) excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share Italy 1910 = 37.1%, 1920 = 41.3%. Low = COW upop/tpop 1915 = 4,014/36,390 = 0.11 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Thompson, The White War (isbn:978-0-571-22333-6), not read from a fetched source. Thompson, The White War ch. 5 and Schindler, Isonzo ch. 2 (isbn 0-275-97204-6): ~35 divisions with ~875,000-1,000,000 men in the field army on 24 May 1915, plus depots, territorial militia and the navy (~40,000). COW milper 1915 = 3,159k is an annual average reflecting later mobilisation and is above the high bound. Snapshot month: May 1915.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Thompson, The White War (isbn:978-0-571-22333-6), not read from a fetched source. Older classes of the mobile and territorial militia not yet called in May 1915; Italy trained only part of each class.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Thompson, The White War (isbn:978-0-571-22333-6), not read from a fetched source. Artillery, engineers, carabinieri with the army, trains, depots, navy.

mobilizationRatio.note: Cited page: 5,615,000 men mobilised (Italian government reply to the ILO, and US War Dept); / ~36.2M = 0.155.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Schindler, Isonzo (isbn:0-275-97204-6), not read from a fetched source. 35 infantry divisions (~12,000 rifles each) plus mobile militia and territorial battalions. Reconstruction from Schindler ch. 2.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Carcano M91 rifle; ~600 MGs in the whole army in May 1915; no wire cutters or helmets

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: conscripts; many reservists from the Libyan war

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Schindler, Isonzo (isbn:0-275-97204-6), not read from a fetched source. Alpini (~78 battalions) and Bersaglieri (12 regiments plus cyclists).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mountain equipment

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: elite mountain and light troops

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Schindler, Isonzo (isbn:0-275-97204-6), not read from a fetched source. 4 cavalry divisions and divisional squadrons (~30 regiments).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: lance and carbine

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: regular cavalry

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Thompson, The White War (isbn:978-0-571-22333-6), not read from a fetched source. ~1,800-2,000 field and mountain guns (75 mm Deport and Krupp) and only ~100-150 modern heavy pieces in May 1915 (Thompson ch. 5).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: good field guns, almost no heavy artillery for the Isonzo

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: ammunition rationed

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Thompson, The White War (isbn:978-0-571-22333-6), not read from a fetched source. ~86 aircraft in the Corpo Aeronautico in May 1915 (Thompson ch. 5), reconnaissance types; Caproni Ca.3 bombers from August 1915.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: French designs, Caproni bombers coming

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: first military use of aircraft in Libya 1911

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's 1906-1921 and checked loosely against the Regia Marina page, not read from a fetched source. Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Conway's 1906-1921 (isbn 0-85177-245-5) and the cited page: 5 dreadnoughts (Dante Alighieri, Conte di Cavour, Giulio Cesare, Leonardo da Vinci, Caio Duilio), ~8 pre-dreadnoughts, ~10 armoured cruisers and ~8 scouts/light cruisers = 27/31/34; plus ~33 destroyers in May 1915 (Conway's) = 30/33/40. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted (MAS boats and torpedo boats stay excluded).

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.65/0.7/0.75 (31) and destroyers 0.55/0.6/0.65 (33), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.75 and 0.5-0.75. Evidence: modern dreadnoughts, fast armoured cruisers, fast destroyers

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers (31) and destroyers (33), both 0.6/0.65/0.7, role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: fleet held back from Austrian minefields and submarines; destroyers in Adriatic raiding

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. ~20 submarines (Conway's).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small Laurenti boats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: coastal operations

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Cadorna's eleven frontal Isonzo offensives, rigid discipline; staff competent at logistics

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: regional conscripts mixed across the country; decimations and harsh discipline; collapse at Caporetto (1917)

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5. Evidence: intervention divisive (Socialists and Catholics opposed); irredentist enthusiasm among the middle class

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: Carcano rifle, 75 mm guns; few MGs and heavy guns

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars, steel helmet 1915). Evidence: Farina body armour, Lancia armoured cars; Adrian helmets from 1916

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnoughts). Evidence: Dante Alighieri the first triple-turret dreadnought; Cavour class

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (concrete forts). Evidence: Alpine forts on the Trentino frontier

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: rail to the Friuli front; teleferiche (cableways) in the Alps

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telegraph, telephone). Evidence: Marconi's country: field radio and telephone

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial reconnaissance. Evidence: aircraft and balloons over the Isonzo

air.note: Anchor: air 7 = 1914-15. Evidence: Caproni Ca.3, the first purpose-built heavy bomber in service

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): Italy 1913 = 4,057, 1914 = 3,835, 1915 = 3,642 (2011 int$). B&H Table 1: 2,564 in 1990 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Low: ~3.5% of GDP before the war; mid: 1915 wartime share; high: 1917-18 peak. B&H give no Italian series (Table 4 note).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry ~25% of output concentrated in the north-west triangle; ~55% of the labour force in agriculture.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Cited page: in 1911, 55.4% of the Italian population worked in agriculture; Economy of fascist Italy page: 56% in 1921. 1 - 0.554 = 0.45 (mid). Italy imported wheat and coal.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching 20 per year (~1.1M births per year in the 1890s, half male, ~65-70% survival).

artillery.note: Cited page: Ansaldo alone built 10,900 artillery pieces during the war; national output per year ~2,000-4,000 by 1917-18.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Fighters per year 1916-1918 (licence Nieuport, SPAD, Hanriot); the cited economic-history page records 3,800 warplanes from Ansaldo alone.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Reconnaissance and Caproni bombers per year 1916-1918; Italian total ~12,000 aircraft over the war.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Capital ships and destroyers per year: Andrea Doria completed 1916, capital ship building then stopped = 0/1/2; destroyers per year 1915-1918 = 3/8/15. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

submarines.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Submarines per year 1915-1918.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. National, provincial and communal roads.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Genoa, Naples, Venice, La Spezia, Taranto, Brindisi, Ancona, Palermo, Livorno.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register returns 1914: Italian flag 1,521,942 GRT (steam and sail, 100 tons and over, Register Book 1913-14). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Static mountain front supplied by rail, lorries and cableways; operational advances rarely beyond ~50 km.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~1.0M horses plus mules and donkeys.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: Alpine barrier and fortified frontier, population support.

notes: Snapshot date 24 May 1915 (declaration of war on Austria-Hungary; mobilisation ordered 22 May, covered earlier by secret call-ups). Territory = the Kingdom of Italy in Europe; Libya, Eritrea, Somalia and the Dodecanese excluded, includes empty. The world_1914 basemap is the nearest file at or before 1915. Aircraft in aircraft_strike (no Italian fighters in May 1915). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Book figures (Thompson, Schindler, Conway's) not fetched online, graded at most B.
